name: Geogaddi
editorial_article: Released in February 2002 on Warp Records, *Geogaddi* is the second studio album by the Scottish electronic duo Boards of Canada, comprising brothers Marcus Eoin and Michael Sandison. Recorded between 1999 and 2001 at the duo's remote Hexagon Sun studio in the Pentland Hills, the album serves as a more claustrophobic, darker, and more complex successor to their seminal 1998 debut, *Music Has the Right to Children*. While the duo's early work was marked by a nostalgic, sun-drenched pastoralism, *Geogaddi* shifts toward the cryptic and the unsettling. \n\nThe creative process for the album was famously obsessive; the duo recorded over 90 tracks, distilling them into a 23-track final sequence that acts as a unified, twisting journey. The sonic palette is deeply textured, characterized by heavily processed analog synths, manipulated acoustic instruments—including flutes and guitars—and an intricate use of sub-frequency layers, backmasking, and subliminal messages. Thematic references throughout the album suggest deep dives into numerology, occultism, pagan folklore, and religious cults, partly inspired by the 1973 horror film *The Wicker Man* and the folk music of The Incredible String Band. Additionally, the production was notably influenced by the ambient national trauma of the September 11 attacks, which deepened the album's inherent paranoia and tension. By blending hauntological dread with meticulous IDM production, *Geogaddi* solidified Boards of Canada's reputation as masters of atmosphere and enigma, and it remains a defining, often scrutinized artifact of early 2000s electronic music.

editorial_pitch: A claustrophobic, dark masterpiece of electronic music, *Geogaddi* is a dense, hypnotic journey through occult-themed analog textures and complex, paranoiac soundscapes. It marks Boards of Canada's definitive turn toward the eerie and the esoteric, cementing their legacy in the IDM canon.
